questions.rawText:
In a signal processing application, two equal-length vectors A and B represent input and weight
values of a digital filter. Each vector contains N elements, and the dot product of these vectors
determines the filter output. Develop a CISC-style assembly program to compute the dot product of
vectors A and B and store the result in memory location DOTPROD. Describe the sequence of
operations required through suitable codes and explanations.

Represent the following numbers in 5-bit 2's complement form, perform the operation mentioned
and state whether overflow occurs or not in each case.
i) Add +9 and +12
ii) Add −8 and −9
Subtract −5 from +10
Implement a three-input XOR gate using 4-to-1 multiplexer with a neat diagram.

Design a sequential circuit with two JK flip-flops A and B and two inputs E and F. If E = 0, the circuit
remains in the same state regardless of the value of F. When E = 1 and F = 1, the circuit goes
through the state transitions from 00 to 01, to 10, to 11, back to 00, and repeats. When E = 1 and F
= 0, the circuit goes through the state transitions from 00 to 11, to 10, to 01, back to 00, and
repeats.
Design a 3-bit synchronous binary up-counter using T flip-flops. Draw the logic diagram.
Write the Verilog code for the K flip flop whose function Table is given below

memory contains 8192 blocks, each consisting of 256 words.
i) How many bits are there in the main memory address?
ii) How many bits are there in each of the TAG, SET, and WORD fields?

i) Distinguish between Uniform Memory Access and Non Uniform Memory Access multi processors.
ii) Explain how cache coherence is maintained in Write-Through and Write-Back protocols.

Perform the addition of the following two 32-bit IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point numbers
and represent the result in IEEE 754 format.
i) A = 0 10000010 10100000000000000000000
ii) B = 0 10000001 11000000000000000000000
Show all the steps including conversion to decimal, exponent alignment, addition, normalization,
and final binary representation.

Apply the concept of microprogramming to explain how a control unit generates control signals
during instruction execution, using a suitable diagram.

performed.

questions.rawText:
Analyze and design a sequential circuit based on the Mealy model that uses D flip-flops to detect
the sequence "0101". The circuit should produce an active high output only when the sequence is
detected and maintain an active low output at all other times. Ensure that the design allows
overlapping of the sequence, meaning that part of one detected sequence can serve as the
beginning of the next.

Illustrate and explain the Three-Bus oriented Register ALU architecture and outline the contrasting
features with that of Two-Bus oriented Register ALU architecture.

Using your understanding of asynchronous counters and SR - flip flops, design a frequency divider
circuit that reduces the system clock frequency by a factor of 1/6. Incorporate the appropriate logic
gates to achieve the desired frequency division.

Design a combinational circuit using 4-bit adder and external gates to add two 4-bit numbers A and
B.
If C < 3, B = 2C,
if C is a multiple of 3, B = C+4,
for all the remaining cases, B = C
Where, C is a 3-bit binary number.
Design a 4X4 combinational shifter using MUX and tristate buffer.
Design G flip flop according to the Table Q2C using NOR latch.
Perform division of (1100)2 by (101)2 using non-restoring division algorithm, indicating all the steps.

Design 2-bit X 2-bit binary multiplier using 3 to 8 decoder with active low output and minimum
external gates.
Design a 2 - bit magnitude comparator using basic gates.

Design a 4-bit synchronous binary counter. Draw the circuit using JK flip-flops and explain how the
flip-flops are connected to count in binary from 0000 to 1111 in synchronization with the clock.

how the state transitions occur with clock inputs.

map and minimize the function.

truth table and logic circuit for the conversion.

Show how to create an 8-to-1 multiplexer by combining two 4-to-1 multiplexers and an additional 2-
to-1 multiplexer

Compare I/O mapped and memory-mapped I/O in terms of address space usage, speed, and
